tests.description: Timed check on Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras

questions.question: Q: What was the Cambrian explosion and why is it important?
questions.correctAnswer: The rapid diversification of life ~541 million years ago, when organisms evolved hard shells and skeletons for the first time. This made fossilisation much more likely, producing an apparent 'explosion' of life in the fossil record. It marks the start of the Palaeozoic Era.

questions.question: Q: How did Coal Measures form in the Carboniferous?
questions.correctAnswer: Vast swamp forests of ferns, horsetails and clubmosses grew in warm, humid conditions. When plants died, they fell into waterlogged swamps where oxygen was absent, preventing decay. Over millions of years, the accumulated plant material was buried, compressed and heated, forming coal seams within sedimentary rock sequences.

questions.question: Q: What caused the Permian-Triassic mass extinction?
questions.correctAnswer: Massive volcanic eruptions of the Siberian Traps released enormous volumes of CO2 and other gases, causing extreme global warming, ocean acidification and anoxia. These environmental changes eliminated ~96% of marine species and ~70% of land species, making it the most severe extinction event in Earth's history.

questions.question: Q: Why are ammonites useful index fossils?
questions.correctAnswer: They evolved rapidly (new species appeared every 1-2 million years), were geographically widespread in marine environments, and had distinctive coiled shells that are easily recognised. Their short time ranges allow precise dating and correlation of Mesozoic rocks worldwide.

questions.question: Q: Name the three periods of the Mesozoic Era in order.
questions.correctAnswer: Triassic (252-201 Ma), Jurassic (201-145 Ma), Cretaceous (145-66 Ma).
